Which tag is which piece of steel

What part 1 settled

  • Every simulator tag has a place on the skid.
  • Photo identifications stay "likely" until the plate is read.

Part 2 · Plant HMI against the model

Does the plant run the way the simulator runs?

Part 2 · the plan

One snapshot, read tag by tag

  1. The operating pointgas only, about 30 % of the design rate
  2. Two HMI screensevery reading against the simulator design state
  3. Eight differenceswhere plant and model part ways
  4. Level bandson/off control against alarms and trips
  5. The P-301 bandon/off feed pressure against the reactor

Part 2 · the operating point

22 Sep 2026, 13:00: gas only, a third of the rate

Ethanol SP 0: a gas-only state, outside the fitted kinetics. The 5 : 1 ratio holds at any litre basis; the absolute rate does not.

Part 2 · two HMI screens

Screen 01: feeds, preheater and reactor1 of 2

Click any box on the screen: plant reading against the simulator design state.

Part 2 · two HMI screens

Screen 02: condenser, separators and utilities2 of 2

TT-609 reads 6.5 °C: the plant chilled water is far colder than the 15 °C the model assumes.

Part 2 · eight differences

Where the plant and the model part ways

Recorded as findings: the validated model is not changed to match one snapshot.

Part 2 · level bands

An on/off level band must sit inside its alarms

Difference 3 in numbers: the drum fills with the valve shut and drains with it open.

Level rises with the valve shut, falls with it open (rates assumed). Both plant bands touch an alarm or a trip every cycle.

Part 2 · the P-301 band

On/off feed pressure against the reactor

The HMI shows SP START and SP STOP: P-301 starts below one pressure and stops above the other.

Feed needs PT-601 + 0.5 bar line loss (assumed). The plant band straddles it and fits PSV-302; the model band fits the C&E but not PSV-302.

Part 2 · summary

What part 2 settled

  • The snapshot is gas only at about 30 % of design.
  • Reactor pressure, bed temperatures and trip setting agree.
  • Controls differ: on/off pump, heaters and levels.
  • Level bands touch alarms; P-301 band straddles the reactor.
  • Gas detection exists; documents need revising.

Part 3 · Inside R-601 and the build

What is inside R-601, and how was the unit built?

Part 3 · the plan

From catalyst pellet to first run

  1. The catalystcomposition and why it must be reduced
  2. Bed loadingfour layers, thermocouples and heater zones
  3. Numbers from the loadingvolume, density, space velocity
  4. The buildworkshop to operation in seven stages

Part 3 · the catalyst

A commercial Cu/ZnO/Al₂O₃ catalyst, loaded as oxides

$$\mathrm{CuO + H_2 \longrightarrow Cu + H_2O}$$

Reduction in place with dilute H₂ before the first feed.

  • Cu: active metal, only after reduction.
  • ZnO: promotes and protects the copper.
  • Al₂O₃: structural support.

5 mm pellets, supplier not named. The model's kg fills the 3.23 m bed.

Part 3 · bed loading

Four layers, three thermocouples, three heater zones

The bed lies on its side here: left is the top, where gas and ethanol enter.

The layers sum to mm against mm stated on the loading sketch: check.

Part 3 · numbers from the loading

Catalyst volume sets the space velocity

catalyst volume, $\tfrac{\pi}{4}D^2h$

mm
$\dot V_E$

mL/min
$$\mathrm{LHSV}=\dfrac{60\,\dot V_E/1000}{V_c}$$

At the plant gas rate with ethanol at design ratio, LHSV would sit near the bottom of the fitted range.

Part 3 · the build

From the workshop to the first run

Each pressure part is tested before it is lifted; hydrogen comes only after leak tests and the C&E function test.

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • The oxide catalyst is reduced in place before feed.
  • Alumina layers distribute flow and hold the pellets.
  • The layer sum differs from the stated total by 82 mm.
  • Fabrication, testing, lifting, completion, then operation.

This deck

Key Takeaways

1

Find every simulator tag on the real skid before operating it.

2

Read a plant snapshot for its state before comparing numbers.

3

Check every on/off band against its alarms and trips.

4

Record plant-model differences as findings; never tune silently.

5

Check loading sketches and documents against each other.
